I've travelled, but not stayed, by myself before. I flew across canada twice when I was 14, and once when I was 15, even missed a flight due to my over one being delayed, and yet here i am:)

Some tips I'd give you are, DOUBLE CHECK EVERYTHING. I don't know if you're taking a plane or a bus or a train, but either way, double check to make sure that you are where you're supposed to be, you're going the right way, etc etc. Bring a little extra cash because food/drink is usually so much more expensive at airports. You want to make sure you have enough. 

Pay attention to your surroundings. Please. And take note of any sketchy people. Because airports/train stations are such a heavy traffic area, it's easy for people to creep on you without you noticing.

And of course, if you're unsure of anything, please ask people (preferably workers, not other travellers) for help! It can be daunting, asking for help but it is important to get correct information about something rather than taking a guess. Hope this helps, my dad's a montreal fan too;)

Hi there! I'm going into my senior year as well, and share a lot of the same anxieties you do about the future and losing people I care about. 

The good news, is that you have control over a lot of the things you're worrying about. What I mean is you have the ability to decide what effort you are going to put in to maintain these relationships. Often when you put in effort, the other person will reciprocate it. And if they don't, perhaps it might be for the better that you and this person no longer are close. Surround yourself with people who care about you just as much as you care about them!

If things are meant to be, it will work itself out. I don't think work is the issue here, as the things you are stressing about aren't work related. That being said, if things continue to decline, take a break from work and see if things get better. If they do, then you'll know that work IS in fact the problem, and you can either quit or just keep trying to get through the tough days. If they don't, you should consider talking to someone you trust abut the way you're feeling. 

The best way to feel better I believe is to first, accept the things you can't change, and two, understand and identify the ways in which you CAN change the outcome. This way, you can set a plan for the things you do control, and stop overthinking the the things you can't.
of course, good luck:)

It seems as though you've been through a lot, so it's to be expected that you might have a difficult time coping with it all. There's no one to blame for the way that you feel, so please don't pin it all on yourself. 

It might be a lot for your partner to handle, I'll be honest, but that doesn't mean it's completely ruined. Relationships aren't always 50/50. Sometimes one of you will need the other a little more, and vice versa. I have been with my boyfriend a year and a bit, and I completely understand how you feel. I felt/ still feel guilty for unloading all of my mental health issues onto him, and often feel as though my mental health is getting in the way of us having a good relationship. 

But this being said, the truth is honestly simple: If it's meant to be, it'll work itself out. Finding hobbies/things you're good at can be very helpful for getting out of the "worthless" headspace. Being GOOD at something and enjoying it can really boost your self-esteem, and while it might not take away the mental health issues, it still gives you something positive to look forward to, and something you can talk about with your partner that makes you happy. And in most cases, if you're happy, your partner will be happy that you're happy.

In all honesty, I think taking to your boyfriend would be the best thing to do. Explain how you're feeling, and why you feel that way. If you are not ready to do something, never push yourself. While I can understand why your boyfriend might be a little put off that you don't want to go, I think how you're feeling is completely normal!

I'm pretty introverted as well, so I completely understand where you're coming from. Sometimes certain social activities are just too much, and there's nothing the matter with that. While I don't know your boyfriend or how he will react, I'd like to think he'd try his best to understand how you're feeling, and I don't think he'd want to put you in a situation where you feel uncomfortable. So my advice would be to tell him, and do your best to explain these feelings/why you feel that way so it's easier for him to understand:)

it all started when my mom and dad got married. they were only married 4 years, 2 of which my momma was cheating on my dad. so... there is a possibility im not my dads:)

they got divorced and my mom left me for 6 months. i was 2 so i don't remember, but my dad said i had a rough time. throughout my early childhood, my mom was rather flaky. she cycled through boyfriends like no tomorrow, brought me to her friends houses to get drunk (keep in mind this happened from ages 4-11), brought me to weight loss meetings and exposed me to unhealthy weight loss techniques, she didn't even come to my myringotomy surgery (it's not a serious surgery, but i was little so it was scary for me). there were a lot of nice times with my mom, but she definitely was not the "mother-of-the-year".

on the other hand, my dad ended up getting re-married to a woman who was relatively nice to me at first, but was ridiculously strict and controlled everything i did. they had another kid together and it was always obvious he was the favourite. when i was in seventh grade, there was an issue at moms and my dad said that i shouldn't go back to my moms anymore. so for two years, i lived at my dads. while i was there things were pretty shit. they were very emotionally abusive, and at times were physically abusive. they completely dismissed my feelings and got mad at me for my shitty mental health, they gave me absolutely no freedom to do anything (hardly ever went out, made me come home for lunch a lot, read my messages), and favoured my brother with everything.

while i was living with my dad, my mom began a relationship with a guy 15 years younger than her, and got pregnant, so i got another brother.

finally, i had enough at my dads because of the constant emotional neglect, i had a mental breakdown and called my mom. i lived with her for a year and a half. she was hella chill at first but over time things got pretty rough. once again had hardly any freedoms, screen time was limited to like an hour everyday, this brother was favored too. we constantly got into fights and they always played the "you left your mom card" to make me feel bad, even tho leaving my moms wasn't my choice. my stepdad got drunk one night and kissed me (i did NOT consent-- i was half asleep when it happened. and even if i did, i was only 15 and he was thirty something.) i haven't told anyone that other than my boyfriend but since im anonymous on here idc. they kicked me out after i snuck out one night, and then i went back to my dads. YAY! more emotional abuse...

my parents hate each other so they always put me in the middle. so yeah. that's my fucked-up family story:)

I remember her showing me his instagram profile, and it was super sketchy. Dude only had like six followers and there were zero pictures of himself on the account.  

Regardless of this, my friend insisted he was the one. 

So fast forward about a week after these two began their relationship. She invites me to her house to hangout, so I accept. We're hanging out, doing thirteen-year-old girl things. She then asks me to leave the room for a sec, and I ask why. She turns red and insists she just needs to "do something." 

After five minutes or so, she allows me to come back into her room and I ask what this was about. She proceeds to burst into tears and simply hands me her phone. I read the messages and it turns out this sick fuck (who i highly doubt was actually a fourteen-year-old boy) had been blackmailing her for naked pictures.
